messages:
Annie (runtime): quick sync — I'm prototyping a different angle on prefix presence to reduce cross-shard RPCs: a small per-shard Bloom presence vector that we rotate by epoch and occasionally reconcile. sketch below, want quick take on correctness tradeoffs and rollout plan.

Max: interesting. how do you handle deletes? blooms are only additive.

Annie (runtime): yeah, main idea is epoch-rotation + short TTL per epoch so absence is eventually consistent. flow: each shard exposes bloom_{epoch} for its resident prefixes; other shards query bloom for a fast "maybe local" test before issuing expensive handoff/RPC/prefetch. on epoch rollover we garbage-collect old blooms.

Ravi: worried about FP causing extra prefetches for cold tenants. what's expected FP rate and memory cost?

Annie (runtime): targeting 0.1% FP with ~256KB per-shard bloom (configurable). worst-case extra prefetches should be bounded; we add a cheap rate-limit on bloom-driven remote prefetch to avoid amplification.

Sasha: what about correctness for hotkey ownership? we shouldn't serve stale positive as authoritative for residency.

Annie (runtime): absolutely — bloom result is advisory only. fallback rules: if bloom says present -> try local fast-path; if local miss then fallback to the canonical shard RPC. if bloom says absent -> skip local fast-path and issue RPC as usual (safe). so we never trust bloom to avoid canonical checks for writes.

Max: can you paste the rough interface?

Annie (runtime): sure — rough pseudocode:

```
// per-shard: expose current epoch bloom (read-only snapshot)
bool maybe_local(prefix) {
  return bloom_current.maybe_contains(prefix);
}

// request handling on remote shard
if (maybe_local(prefix)) {
  // fast try local cache read
  res = local_cache.get(prefix);
  if (res) return res; // success
  // fallthrough to canonical RPC
}
res = rpc_to_owner(prefix);
return res;
```

Ravi: seems fine; what about evictions? if owner evicts but bloom still reports positive until epoch changes, other shards may hammer the owner with prefetch attempts. Add backoff?

Annie (runtime): plan is to combine three mitigations: 1) short epochs (30s-2m configurable) so false positives clear quickly; 2) bloom-driven prefetches are rate-limited per-tenant and use exponential backoff on repeated misses; 3) owner exposes small eviction counters in telemetry so we can detect and throttle cross-shard prefetch to a shard under eviction pressure.

Sasha: and cross-data-center traffic? we'll need separate blooms per-region to avoid extra WAN costs.

Annie (runtime): yes, region-local blooms by default. remote-region shards can still fetch bloom snapshots on demand but we won't poll them frequently.

Max: operation-wise, how would rollout look? I want a safe canary path.

Annie (runtime): rollout plan: 1) opt-in feature flag per-cluster exposing bloom snapshots; 2) start with read-only advisory path: bloom only gates an extra local fast-path (no change to canonical RPC behavior) — this is what I described; 3) monitor metrics: false-positive prefetch rate, owner RPC increase, eviction-led saturation. 4) A/B at 10% traffic then 50% then global.

Ravi: metrics to add: bloom_maybe_count, bloom_miss_after_maybe, bloom_prefetch_rps, owner_eviction_rate, per-tenant_prefetch_backoff_count.

Annie (runtime): added to the list. also propose a small gauge: bloom_epoch_skew to detect shards running stale epochs.

Sasha: how do we sign/verify bloom snapshots? do we need auth to avoid poisoning?

Annie (runtime): snapshots pulled over mTLS between runtime nodes; we'll include an epoch signature and a sequence id. integrity is important — no anonymous pulls.

Max: perf question — building blooms every epoch could be costly on high-churn shards. can we incrementally update a Cuckoo filter or use a rolling counting bloom?

Annie (runtime): good call. two implementation options: 1) rebuild per epoch from residency table (simpler, heavier), 2) maintain an incremental counting-bloom and emit compressed diffs per epoch. start with rebuild for correctness, then optimize to diffs if CPU/memory shows up.

Ravi: sounds reasonable as long as we guard rebuild during GC windows.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary/bloom-presence v1 -> eng-runtime-canary at 2245123480 by annie-ci (status: pending).

Sasha: last: can bloom snapshot leaks reveal tenant residency patterns? any privacy concern?

Annie (runtime): potential info leak: bloom presence reveals that a prefix was recently resident. mitigate by hashing prefixes with a per-cluster salt before inserting into bloom and by keeping small false-positive rates so single-prefix inference is hard. also restrict snapshot distribution to cluster nodes only.

Max: OK. my +1 for prototype in canary mode. keep it advisory-only and add all telemetry.

Annie (runtime): thanks — I'll open a short RFC and a prototype PR this week. actionable items: create RFC, implement snapshot endpoint (read-only), add metrics, feature-flag gate.

Ravi: I'll help with the telemetry dashboard queries.

Sasha: I'll review security bits for snapshot auth and prefix hashing.

Annie (runtime): cool — will post short RFC link when drafted.
